Then, it focuses on the basic framework of learning-based 3D reconstruction approaches, their improvement directions, and their applications in fruits and other agricultural products. In addition, the challenges encountered in fruit 3D reconstruction, such as occlusion and complex lighting conditions, are summarized, along with potential solutions. Finally, future research directions are discussed. This review serves as a valuable reference for promoting the integration of computer vision and agricultural intelligence and advancing the fruit industry chain’s digital and intelligent transformation.

title: High-precision tobacco phenotype extraction based on 3D point clouds
abstract: As an economically important crop, tobacco requires the precise extraction of phenotypic characterization data, which is crucial for breeding, cultivation practices, physiological research, and industrial applications. However, there is currently a lack of automated algorithms for extracting key basic phenotypic traits such as plant height, leaf number, leaf area, and stem-leaf angle. In this study, we developed a set of computational methods for fully automated extraction of these phenotypic features from 3D tobacco point cloud data. Specifically, our pipeline includes: (1) preprocessing the 3D point cloud data, involving operations such as downsampling, denoising, normal vector estimation, and coordinate transformation; (2) integrating a graph neural network with a region-growing algorithm to segment leaves, stems, and other organs, and refining the segmentation results to address the challenge of overlapping leaves; and (3) calculating fundamental phenotypic attributes including plant height, leaf count, leaf area, and stem-leaf angle based on the segmentation output. Additionally, to address potential gaps in the scanned point cloud, we implemented perforation detection and repair operations. The effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed algorithm were validated through mathematical model simulations. Distinct from traditional statistical discriminative methods, this approach provides a novel framework for the precise extraction of tobacco phenotypic data.

title: HDC-Net: A hierarchical detection and counting framework for apple aphids with density-level classification
abstract: To address the challenge of accurately detecting and counting apple aphids across varying density scenarios, this study proposes a hierarchical detection and counting framework named HDC-Net. The framework integrates the YOLO-Aphid model for object detection and the MCNN model for density estimation and counting. It aims to achieve precise recognition and quantification of apple aphids under complex orchard conditions. Initially, an apple aphid image dataset was constructed and optimized, with slice-based preprocessing and the ESRGAN super-resolution technique employed to enhance image quality. A novel density classification method based on multi-source feature fusion and secondary decision rules was developed, enabling accurate categorization of aphid density levels and supporting adaptive model selection. For low-density scenarios, a customized detection model—YOLO-Aphid was designed by incorporating a small-object detection layer, embedding the Swin Transformer attention mechanism, and employing the MPDIoU loss function. These enhancements significantly improved the model’s capability to detect small-scale targets. In the medium- and high-density scenarios, a pixel-level regression strategy based on MCNN was adopted to generate density maps, effectively handling target overlap and occlusion. Furthermore, key parameters of the adaptive Gaussian kernel were fine-tuned via NSGA-III, enhancing counting accuracy under dense distributions. Experimental results demonstrated that in low-density conditions, the YOLO-Aphid model achieved a precision (P) of 96.4 %, recall (R) of 95.2 %, and average precision (AP) of 97.7 %, surpassing the baseline YOLOv8 by 6.1 %, 6.1 %, and 5.9 %, respectively. In the medium- and high-density scenes, the MCNN model reached a mean absolute error (MAE) of 5.01 and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 6.39. These results validate the superior performance of HDC-Net in accurately detecting and counting apple aphids, offering a scientific foundation and methodological reference for intelligent pest monitoring and precision control in orchard environments.

title: Opportunities and challenges in the application of Digital Twins for orchard management
abstract: Digital Twins (DTs) represent a new tool for enabling data-driven orchard management, with the goal of optimizing resource allocation and decision-making. However, unlike general agriculture or annual horticultural systems, fruit tree production is constrained by fixed seasonal cycles, making it difficult to conduct experiments or interventions outside these periods. In addition, the perennial nature of fruit trees, along with complex canopy structures and long production cycles, further increases the complexity and variability of orchard management. An orchard DT consists of a virtual counterpart of the physical orchard entity, with real-time integration of sensor data and a model allowing predictions of system behavior. DTs have the potential to cover all stages of tree-fruit production, from cultivation to post-harvest. This review article of the literature up to 2025 systematically summarizes and indicates that the application of DTs in orchard management remains in an exploratory stage, reflecting the state of development and adoption of enabling technologies, such as the Internet of Things, artificial intelligence, cloud computing, edge computing, extended reality, communications, and blockchain. DTs have been developed for orchard establishment, operations, harvest forecast and optimization, robotic harvesting, natural disaster response, and orchard inventory, with the dominant focus being on harvest operations. Additionally, DTs have been applied to optimize specific orchard processes, such as modelling spray droplet movement within canopies in support of the design of spraying equipment. Very few applications have involved a control system. Commonalities observed in the development of existing orchard DT models suggest the potential for a standardized or universal DT model to support expanded automation operations. Beyond routine orchard management, the potential application of DTs in areas such as natural disaster response is also highlighted, offering opportunities for cost sharing and broader cross-sector benefits.

title: Rapid path definition and path-tracking method of CleaningBot in stacked cage farming houses based on learning from demonstration
abstract: Autonomous navigation within confined stacked cage farming houses (SCFHs) poses several challenges: repetitive structures negatively impact the performance of scan-matching-based simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM); vision-based systems are impeded by weak textures from mesh cages, motion blur, and lighting variations; and the long-term reliability of fiducial markers is compromised by harsh dusty conditions. To address these challenges, this study introduces a comprehensive map-free navigation framework implemented in CleaningBot, a two-wheeled differential-drive autonomous mobile robot. Central to this framework is a novel learning-oriented algorithm for rapid path definition. By employing the learning from demonstration (LfD) method, CleaningBot captures key action points and directional angles, enabling path definition within minutes based on a single human demonstration, which is a substantial improvement over manual waypointing, a process that can take more than 50 min. For precise path execution, a feedback linearization straight-line tracking controller was used to minimize the lateral and angular deviations. This was integrated with a reactive obstacle avoidance controller to form an adaptive path and obstacle navigation controller (APONC). The system’s robustness relies on a high-precision inertial localization module, enhanced by an improved University of Michigan benchmark (UMBmark)-based odometry calibration method. Extensive experiments confirmed the performance of the system, highlighting three key achievements: (1) The robot achieved a positioning error of only 0.053 % over a 500 m trajectory, significantly outperforming common SLAM-based methods in degraded settings. (2) In real SCFH environments, trajectory reproduction achieved overlap rates of more than 99 %. (3) The APONC enabled the robot to avoid a moving person and realign with its path in 3.2 s, with a final residual lateral error of only 0.031 m. This study presents a practical, efficient, and robust navigation solution for confined agricultural environments.

title: Precise identification of noxious weeds in alpine meadows using UAV-based hyperspectral remote sensing with multi-feature integration and deep learning
abstract: The spread of noxious weeds in alpine meadows threatens grassland productivity and biodiversity. Accurate identification is challenging because both weeds and native grasses are low-growing and vegetation is highly heterogeneous. High-resolution UAV hyperspectral imagery is a valuable data source for fine-scale ecological monitoring. To accurately identify noxious weeds in alpine meadows, this study extracted spectral, textural, and geometric features, and applied Mahalanobis distance with RFECV to select key spectral bands, constructing an optimized multi-feature dataset. The performance of multiple machine learning and deep learning models, including Random Forest and 3D-CNN, is systematically compared to achieve fine-scale and high-accuracy identification. The results show that: (1) Noxious weeds (Elsholtzia densa Benth and Aconitum gymnandrum Maxim) exhibit significant differences in the first and second derivatives within the 650–800 nm wavelength range, as well as in the 550 nm region of the derivative envelope spectra; (2) In the multi-feature variable set constructed from the sensitive bands selected based on RFECV and Mahalanobis distance, spectral indices contribute 64.98% (with NGNDVI, RENDVI, and SR being the most significant), while MNF and continuum removal contribute 12.27% and 8.72%, respectively; (3) Among nine identification models, the 3D-CNN model achieved the best overall recognition performance for noxious weeds, with an overall accuracy (OA) of up to 99.55% and a Kappa coefficient of 0.9929. This study demonstrates the potential of multi-feature fusion combined with deep learning for fine-grained identification of noxious weeds, providing high-precision technical support for ecological restoration of alpine meadows.

title: Marine aquaculture biological object detection based on color-line image enhancement and improved YOLOv7 model
abstract: Underwater images suffer from hazing degradation because of the special underwater imaging process. To achieve clear and accurate detection results of marine aquaculture biological object, an aquaculture biological detection method based on color-line image enhancement and improved YOLOv7 model is proposed in this paper. Firstly, underwater image enhancement method is proposed to solve the degradation problem based on color-line method for dehazing and color correction to enhance contrast. Secondly, a marine aquaculture biological object detection method based on YOLOv7 is presented. We construct a marine aquaculture biological dataset including 5455 images with four categories: echinus, holothurian, scallop and starfish. Finally, a dual-attention module is designed to extract object features. The dual-attention which combines adaptive channel attention and spatial supplement attention applies to YOLOv7. The experimental results show that the mAP is 87.4% and the speed has reaching 49.3 FPS. This method can achieve clear, real-time and accurate detection of marine aquaculture organisms, providing effective guidance for real-time monitoring and scientific breeding of marine aquaculture.

title: BSRNet: a novel neural network for broiler chicken sound signal recognition used in health monitoring
abstract: Accurate and effective health monitoring methods for broiler chickens are crucial for the development of modern agriculture and the promotion of agricultural income. Recent studies have primarily focused on broiler sounds, using signal processing algorithms to extract physical information from sound signals, and employing meticulous and specialized extra preprocessing methods to generate high-quality feature datasets. This dataset then serves as the input for a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to establish a sound signal recognition model, thereby facilitating indirect health monitoring of broiler chickens. However, the high specialization and complexity of extra preprocessing techniques pose significant challenges to the scalability and universality of practical applications. Moreover, CNNs inherently lack the autonomy to identify core features, preventing the network from effectively modeling using the most distinctive features. Additionally, the model’s inability to perform flexible nonlinear mappings based on the specificity of the information captured by the convolutional kernels restricts the network’s capability to abstractly represent complex nonlinear relationships and local sound patterns of broiler chickens. These limitations constrain the accuracy of broiler chicken health monitoring. To address these issues, this paper introduces a novel Broiler Sound Recognition Network (BSRNet), which includes innovative components such as Separated Convolution (SepConv) and Adaptive Pre-activated Convolution (APAConv), along with a feature fusion structure (DFF). The proposed SepConv convolution allows the network to autonomously recognize key core features through a feature separation and recombination mechanism, avoiding the limitations associated with cumbersome denoising, filtering, and other extra preprocessing methods. The APAConv, through adaptive pre-activation, performs adaptive nonlinear mappings based on the characteristics of different types of local sound patterns captured by the convolutional kernels, enhancing the network’s ability to express complex nonlinear relationships. The DFF structure utilizes both novel convolutions to transform feature channel dimensions (expansion and compression) to achieve multilevel feature fusion and abstract representation. The authors collected a large dataset of broiler chicken sound signals and created four datasets using signal processing algorithms, then conducted comparative experiments with eight methods, achieving competitive results that demonstrate the superiority and advancement of BSRNet. Additionally, ablation experiments validated the effectiveness of BSRNet’s core components. Finally, the authors employed T-SNE, Grad-CAM++, and feature visualization techniques for a detailed interpretability analysis of the methods discussed in this paper.

title: HanwooReID: Multi-view cattle re-identification with pose-aware transformer enhancements
abstract: Identifying individual Hanwoo cattle automatically is particularly challenging: Hanwoo cattle exhibit highly similar visual characteristics, and unlike pedestrian re-identification, cattle undergo dramatic changes in appearance and scale as their poses and camera viewpoints vary. To address these challenges, we introduce HanwooReID, a large-scale multi-view dataset collected on real farms, comprising 9,929 images of 31 cattle captured under diverse viewpoints, poses, and lighting conditions. Building on this dataset, we propose a transformer-based framework that integrates a pose-guided heatmap encoder (PHE) to focus attention on identity-relevant regions and a viewpoint-constrained retrieval (VCR) strategy that projects hoof keypoints onto a bird’s-eye view (BEV) plane to estimate cattle orientation. This BEV-based orientation estimation effectively filters out gallery candidates with inconsistent viewpoints, substantially improving matching accuracy under severe pose and view variations. Extensive experiments on both closed-set and open-set protocols show that our method outperforms existing baselines, achieving up to 7.4% and 6.8% improvements in mean Average Precision (mAP), respectively, demonstrating its effectiveness for precision livestock farming.

title: Design and test of potato plot breeding hole sowing device based on MATLAB and MFBD simulation
abstract: To address the challenges in China’s potato plot seeding process, such as low mechanisation rates, high labour intensity, and the incompatibility of existing planters with plot seeding operations, a planar seed-carrying and hole-sowing device has been designed for self-propelled potato plot planter. Based on establishing the constraints of the planar seed-carrying hole sowing device, combined with the kinematic model of the mechanism, the human–computer interaction visualisation auxiliary design assistant software was developed with the MATLAB APP Designer platform; through this software, the parameters of each component within the hole sowing device were optimised, yielding optimal trajectory characteristics. Additionally, a safety analysis of the designed burrowing device was conducted using the FFlex function in Recurdyn to confirm the reliability of its structure. Bench tests were carried out, and the motion trajectory of the burrower was tracked and collected using a high-speed camera test bench, and the motion trajectory parameters of the mechanism were proved to meet the requirements through analysis; the field sowing verification test showed that when the machine operated at different speeds of 0.3 m·s−1, 0.4 m·s−1, and 0.5 m·s−1, the re-sowing rate ranged from 3.44 % to 4.21 %; the miss-sowing rate ranged from 3.60 % to 4.49 %; the coefficient of variation of the plant spacing ranged from 4.27 % to 5.60 %; the sowing depth qualification rate ranged from 93.65 % to 94.82 %, which further verified that the designed hole sowing device could meet the quality requirements of sowing operation in potato plot breeding.

title: Optimizing and applying the CSM-CERES-Maize model for enhanced maize yield and nitrogen management in Florida sandy soils
authors: Diego Arruda Huggins de Sã Leitão
abstract: Nitrogen (N) management is critical for maize production on sandy soils with warm subtropical climates due to the high risk of nitrate-N (NO3-N) leaching, which poses environmental challenges. Thus, developing best management practices is essential to sustain yields while minimizing ecological impacts. This study aimed to calibrate and evaluate the CSM-CERES-Maize model for the Pioneer 1870 hybrid maize cultivar and apply it to analyze yield gaps and assess the effects of N rates on yield and NO3-N leaching. Field experiments were conducted in Live Oak, north Florida, on irrigated sandy soils during 2022 and 2023, testing six N rates (0–392 kg N ha−1) in 78.5 kg N ha−1 increments. The model was calibrated and evaluated using field data, and its performance was assessed by comparing predictions with observed values. Calibration results showed high agreement for aboveground biomass [index of agreement (d) = 0.99, relative root mean square error (RRMSE) = 11.6%], aboveground biomass N (d = 0.99, RRMSE = 11.3%), and NO3-N leaching (d = 0.99, RRMSE = 12.9%). Model evaluation indicated reliable predictions for grain yield [coefficient of determination (R2) = 0.81), grain N (R2 = 0.85), aboveground biomass (d = 0.87–0.99, RRMSE = 16–47%], aboveground biomass N (d = 0.83–0.99, RRMSE = 9–45%), and NO3-N leaching (d = 0.67–0.95, RRMSE = 24.3–77.7%). The model also demonstrated varying degrees of agreement in estimating soil NO3-N (d = 0.43–0.99, RRMSE = 31–118 %), total soil inorganic N (d = 0.55–0.94, RRMSE = 37–118%), and soil water content (d = 0.33–0.71, RRMSE = 13–63%). Long-term simulations showed that using N rates below 235 kg ha−1 resulted in significant yield reductions (up to 80%) but significantly decreased NO3-N leaching (27%). Increasing N rates above 235 kg ha−1 led to insignificant yield improvements (2%) while significantly raising NO3-N leaching by 40%. The highest yield gaps resulted from combined N and water stress (82%) but could be reduced to 29% with optimal N and irrigation management. The study highlights the effectiveness of the CSM-CERES-Maize model in optimizing N rates to balance yield and environmental impact in north Florida. Future research should explore narrower N rate intervals and different N sources and application methods to refine best management practices.

title: Evaluation of carbon footprint effect in land consolidation for sustainable agricultural planning: A research on transportation and intra-parcel tractor maneuvers
abstract: Carbon emission is a major driver to climate change, posing significant challenges to global sustainability efforts. Agriculture, as a key sector, plays a substantial role in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, with land fragmentation further exacerbating this issue by increasing fuel consumption and CO2 emissions during farming activities. Land consolidation (LC) has emerged as an effective strategy to mitigate these impacts by reducing the spatial dispersion of parcels and improving mechanization efficiency. This study focuses on a consolidation area in Konya, a vital agricultural region in Türkiye. It examines the effects of changes in routes and tractor maneuvers before and after LC on the fuel consumption of tractors and, accordingly, the carbon footprint (CF). Using network analysis and the Tier-1 method for CF calculations, the study found a 40% reduction in total CO2 emissions due to decreased transportation distances. The average CF per enterprise decreased by 38.26%, demonstrating the potential of LC to make a substantial contribution to GHG reduction. These findings highlight LC’s role in fostering sustainable agricultural planning and environmental conservation, providing a pathway for long-term carbon reduction and climate resilience. Further research is recommended to develop region-specific LC models integrating socio-economic and climatic variables for enhanced sustainability outcomes.

title: Modeling and temporal analysis of electrical impedance spectroscopy responses of Rosa chinensis under powdery mildew stress
abstract: Under the intensifying impact of global climate change, the frequency of plant disease outbreaks is steadily increasing, posing significant challenges to healthy cultivation and precision management. To enable early diagnosis of plant disease stress, this study used two rose (Rosa chinensis) varieties, ’Red Cap’ and ’Carefree Wonder’ were used to conduct powdery mildew stress experiment. Throughout the stress period, leaf electrical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), physiological parameters, and ultrastructural observations, were collected. A novel lumped equivalent circuit model was proposed, incorporating plant cell electrophysiological properties. The model developed for both rose varieties-featuring Constant Phase Elements (CPE) and Warburg elements (W), successfully characterized the resistive properties of the leaf tissue, including the extracellular resistance (R1), cell membrane resistance (R2), intracellular resistance (R3), and vacuole interior resistance (R4). Model parameters R1 and R3 were significantly correlated with the above physiological indicators, and showed significant differences 3 to 11 days earlier than traditional physiological parameters, demonstrating strong potential for early detection of cellular damage. Overall, this study demonstrates that EIS technology can dynamically reflect electrical property changes in plant tissues under biotic stress, effectively overcoming the lag limitations of conventional physiological measurements, providing a promising tool for early disease diagnosis and resistance screening.

title: Agriculture Machine fault detection based on multiple Input-Parallel-Neural network optimized by genetic algorithm with matrix chromosomes
abstract: Accurate and efficient fault detection in agricultural machinery is essential for minimizing downtime and preventing costly failures. Conventional single-input neural network approaches often face limitations, requiring extensive preprocessing and yielding suboptimal accuracy. This paper introduces a novel framework that integrates a genetic algorithm (GA) with matrix chromosome encoding to automatically design and optimize multi-input, parallel convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for advanced fault diagnostics. This approach automates the design and optimization of the network for advanced fault detection. Unlike typical vector-based approaches, this method uses matrix chromosomes to encode the entire CNN architecture. Separate chromosomes represent different aspects of the network, including hyperparameters, network configuration, and learning settings. This allows the genetic algorithm to simultaneously explore, tune, and optimize these variables. The parallel structure of the CNNs is leveraged to enhance fault detection accuracy and efficiency. The evolved parallel CNNs demonstrate superior performance compared to traditional singular-network models. In experimental tests, they achieved an outstanding accuracy of 99.99% in distinguishing up to 22 different state classes. This method also reduces the size of the networks and the number of required data sensors while minimizing the need for data preprocessing. The integration of GAs with parallel CNNs presents a promising direction for future research in various rotating machine configurations.

title: A collaborative and low cost acquisition chain for collecting spatialized observations in agriculture
abstract: This technical note describes a new data acquisition chain for real-time collection and sharing of georeferenced observations made manually and recorded on a form using a smartphone for agriculture projects. This acquisition chain relies on a low-cost RTK GNSS rover and the open source Centipede network to obtain corrected geolocation with centimeter accuracy on any Android smartphone device. The Mergin Maps application, which completes this acquisition chain, provides versatility making it possible to design custom projects to meet a large diversity of applications in agriculture (collection of quantitative or qualitative data, images, polygons etc.). The precision provided by these technologies can also be easily combined with existing tools for collaborative data collection. The observations made through this application can be shared in real time with other users involved in the project, even remotely. The simplicity of use of this acquisition chain paves the way for ambitious data acquisition campaigns in agriculture which could involve a large number of participants with different profiles and/or take place over a wide variety of scales (field, domain, cooperative, region, etc.). Two case-studies, which led to the collection of several thousand observations, are presented to demonstrate the potential of this acquisition chain. The first case study deals with mapping missing and dead vines on a 35 ha vineyard, it highlights the flexibility of the acquisition chain and the convenience for sharing data. The second case study highlights the collaborative potential of the acquisition chain with more than thirty participants simultaneously involved in a one day project to make observations of vineyard yields performed at the field level.

title: A finite element-MPC framework for optimizing energy-water footprint in direct-seeded rice with straw return practices in rice–wheat rotations
abstract: Intensified rice–wheat rotations increase greenhouse gas emissions through straw incorporation and puddled transplanted rice. While combining rotary straw return with furrow-irrigated, directly dry-seeded rice (DDR) shows promise in mitigating emissions, a decision support tool to guide such practices remains underdeveloped. Such a tool is essential for optimizing energy and water footprints, methane (CH4) emission risks, and tailwater reuse. Moreover, the mechanistic basis for integrating these optimizations with water conservation practices remains unclear. Therefore, this study proposes a finite element (FE)-model predictive control (MPC) framework, developed by coupling Hydrus 2D/3D with a closed-loop optimal model. The system is designed to optimize energy costs and water use in DDR under straw return and varying field conditions, including bare soil, biodegradable film mulching, and tailwater reuse. Experimental validation, data collection, and field case studies were conducted in Babaiqiao, Nanjing, China, during 2023 and 2024 seasons. These activities included rotary straw incorporation, furrow-ridge layouts, dry-seeded rice cultivation, soil hydraulic experiments, tailwater recovery and reuse, and relevant agronomic management. Hydrus 2D/3D effectively simulated wetting rates and soil moisture content for bare and film-mulched ridges, at R2 of 0.79 and 0.89, and 0.80 and 0.90, respectively. Predictive control and tailwater reuse had statistically significant (p < 0.05) effects on energy and water consumption. Integrating film mulching with the FE-MPC framework reduced cumulative water use by 38.0 %. When applied with tailwater reuse, the system offset up to 34.9 % of freshwater demand. In bare furrow-ridge, the controller achieved energy cost savings of up to 32.8 and 41.8 % without and with tailwater reuse, respectively. Film mulching increased energy savings by 53.7 and 62.7 % compared to conventional alternating wetting and drying. The study provides practical strategies, which optimize energy costs and mitigate soil anoxia and tailwater-related pollution risks, thereby reducing the environmental footprint of rice–wheat rotations.

title: Progress in applications of self-supervised learning to computer vision in agriculture: A systematic review
abstract: Precision Agriculture (PA) has emerged as an approach to optimize production, comprise different technology and principles focusing on how to improve agricultural production. Currently, one of the main foundations of PA is the use of artificial intelligence, through deep learning (DL) algorithms. By processing large volumes of complex data, DL enhances decision-making and boosts farming efficiency. However, these methods are hungry for annotated data, which contrasts with the scarce availability of annotated agricultural data and the costs of annotation. Self-supervised learning (SSL) has emerged as a solution to tackle the lack of annotated agricultural data. This study presents a review of the application of SSL methods to computer vision tasks in the agricultural context. The aim is to create a starting point for professionals and scientists who intend to apply these methods using agricultural data. The results of 33 studies found in the literature are discussed, highlighting their pros and cons. In most of the studies, SSL outperformed its supervised counterpart, using datasets from 4000 to 60,000 samples. Potential directions for improving future research are suggested.

title: Precision nitrogen management for maize based on crop modeling, remote sensing and machine learning
abstract: The simultaneous improvement of crop yield and nitrogen (N) use efficiency (NUE) can be potentially achieved through precision N management. In this study, crop modeling, remote sensing, and machine learning were combined to develop and assess a precision N recommendation strategy (MSM-PNM) for maize (Zea mays L.) based on twenty-eight site-years of field experiments conducted in Northeast China involving various N rates and planting densities. For the MSM-PNM strategy, a crop growth model was used at the eight-leaf stage of maize to initially predict the in-season optimal side-dressing N rate (EOSN) by combining current season’s available weather data prior to side-dressing with weather data from previous years for the remaining growing period. Maize N status was then estimated using machine learning models based on data collected with an active canopy sensor along with weather, soil, and management information. Finally, the crop model predicted EOSN was adjusted using the estimated maize N status. The prediction accuracy of EOSN (R2 = 0.70, root mean squared error (RMSE) = 18.60 kg ha−1) based on this integrated MSM-PNM strategy was higher than using crop model only (R2 = 0.65, RMSE = 20.10 kg ha−1). The precision maize management system based on the integrated MSM-PNM strategy decreased N rates by 6–16 % and increased NUE by 8–18 % over farmer practice applying 250 kg N ha−1 as basal N fertilizer without side-dress N application and regional optimal management practice applying split N at fixed rate and timing, while maintaining high grain yield and marginal net return. It is concluded that this new integrated precision N management strategy combining the advantages of crop modeling, remote sensing, and machine learning can significantly increase maize NUE while maintaining high crop yield, thus contributing to food security and agricultural sustainability.

title: Enhanced audio-based fish feeding intensity recognition via decomposed visually-guided cross-modality distillation
abstract: Fish feeding intensity recognition (FFIR) is crucial for sustainable aquaculture management and production optimization. Acoustic-based methods offer non-invasive, cost-effective monitoring in turbid water conditions where visual systems fail. However, acoustic signals struggle to capture temporal behavioral dynamics (such as fish movement patterns) and spatial motion patterns (such as fish aggregation and swimming trajectories) easily detected by visual systems, limiting their discriminative capability for behavioral analysis. This limitation results in a significant performance gap between the best acoustic methods and visual approaches. To address these challenges, we propose AquaDistill, a novel cross-modal knowledge distillation framework that enhances audio-only systems by transferring knowledge from visual modalities during training while requiring only acoustic input during inference. AquaDistill incorporates a decomposed distillation strategy that separates audio features into static acoustic and dynamic behavioral branches, with hybrid distillation losses enabling effective motion knowledge transfer while avoiding feature entanglement. In addition, we introduce the cross-modal behavioral fusion (CMBF) mechanism that leverages distillation-guided knowledge to preserve temporal locality crucial for behavioral analysis through adaptive feature enhancement and cross-branch information exchange. Unlike conventional distillation methods that directly inject cross-modal knowledge, our framework maintains feature separation throughout the learning process while enabling intelligent fusion of complementary acoustic representations. Experimental results demonstrate that AquaDistill significantly improves audio-only model performance, achieving 89 % mean average precision (mAP) and 87 % accuracy, representing improvements of 7 % and 5 % respectively compared to baseline approaches, while maintaining exceptional computational efficiency with only 5.9 M parameters and 1.4 ms inference time. This effectively bridging the performance gap between acoustic and visual methods while maintaining the deployment advantages of audio-only systems. Our enhanced acoustic-based approach demonstrates significant potential for practical aquaculture monitoring applications.

title: Intelligent technologies in poultry farming: a review of smart breeding and precision production
abstract: Integrating IoT, machine vision, and deep learning, intelligent technologies are transforming poultry farming by enabling precision management and improving welfare. This review synthesizes findings from over 200 publications published in the past five years, aiming to clarify the current status, advancements, and key challenges in environmental control, health monitoring, and production performance assessment in poultry farming. In terms of environmental regulation, the integration of computational fluid dynamics (CFD)-based temperature–humidity synergy systems with infrared thermal imaging provides a way for markedly improving thermal comfort for poultry. In health monitoring, multimodal approaches, notably acoustic and gait analysis, enable early detection of respiratory and leg disorders. In evaluating production performance, non-contact body weight estimation and non-destructive egg quality assessment technologies are approaching commercialization. Recent research has increasingly focused on cutting-edge innovations, including optimization of multiphysics coupling systems based on digital twins, edge computing for real-time decision-making, and blockchain-enabled frameworks for enhancing transparency and traceability. Despite these advancements, high sensor network costs and insufficient algorithmic robustness remain key obstacles to the large-scale industrial application of intelligent poultry systems. To promote sustainable development in the poultry industry, future research should focus on modeling disease–environment–behavior interactions, developing affordable and adaptable sensing technologies, and strengthening interdisciplinary collaboration.

title: Apple diameter prediction during mechanical picking based on flexible force-sensing and CNN-BiLSTM-Attention method
abstract: Fruit diameter grading is essential for commercialization, packaging, and market sales, directly impacting the value and competitiveness of fruits. Traditional diameter grading is typically performed after harvesting, relying on manual or mechanical methods. This process introduces extra steps and increases the risk of fruit damage during transit, which can reduce economic efficiency. To address this issue, this study introduces a real-time apple diameter grading method utilizing a flexible force-sensing gripper and the CNN-BiLSTM-Attention deep learning network, enabling synchronized intelligent identification and grading of apple diameter during robotic mechanical picking. First, ionogel-based triboelectric nanogenerators (IG-TENG) were developed and mounted on the surface of a three-finger Fin-Ray flexible picking end effector. A contact force monitoring system was established using a modular apple model, and the force sensor was calibrated. This setup allowed for accurate measurement of the contact force between the fingers and the apple. Using a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) to integrate mechanical response data, robotic hand motor stroke, and apple posture information, an apple contact force model was created to accurately predict the actual gripping force under various grasping conditions. Finally, a CNN-BiLSTM-Attention diameter prediction model was designed to deliver real-time, precise fruit diameter estimates. Orchard experiments demonstrated that the apple diameter grading method, combining force sensing with deep learning, achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 2.13 mm and a grading accuracy of 92 %, supporting non-destructive gripping and accurate grading. This research addresses the limitations of traditional diameter grading methods, streamlines harvesting steps, enhances efficiency, and offers a cost-effective and reliable solution for non-destructive fruit diameter grading.

title: Accuracy and accessibility in soil color determination: A comparative analysis of Munsell Chart, colorimeter, and smartphone in Amazonian soils
abstract: Soil color is a key diagnostic property and fundamental morphological characteristic that provides valuable insights into its properties and pedological processes, and is widely used in the taxonomic classification of soils. However, traditional methods of soil color determination, such as the Munsell color chart, are limited by the subjectivity of visual interpretation, which can lead to significant variations in results. This study aimed to compare the accuracy of soil RGB (Red, Green, Blue) color parameters obtained by three distinct methods: Munsell color chart, colorimeter, and smartphone, with a focus on minimizing subjectivity and improving measurement reliability in Amazonian soils. We analyzed 98 samples from Capanema, Pará (Brazil), collected from two layers (0.00–0.20 m and 0.20–0.40 m) under both dry and moist conditions. Data were processed using Spearman correlation, ANOVA, and Lin’s concordance correlation coefficient. Results showed that the Munsell color chart exhibited the highest variability and poorest agreement, particularly in moist conditions and deeper layers. The colorimeter and smartphone showed superior consistency, with smartphone imaging proving to be a viable, low-cost field alternative. Digital soil color analysis via smartphones significantly reduced measurement subjectivity and uncertainty. Results demonstrate that smartphone-based color analysis offers a reliable method for Amazonian soils, effectively converting common devices into precise scientific tools for agricultural and environmental management. This mobile approach enables standardized field measurements in resource-limited settings, representing an innovative advancement for soil characterization and digital tools, particularly in Amazon biome.

title: SP-DETR: Superior point weak semi-supervised DETR with teacher–student paradigm for crop and weed detection
abstract: Recent years have witnessed extensive applications of deep learning-based computer vision techniques in agriculture for efficient digital management. Among these applications, field crop detection has emerged as a key research focus in smart agriculture. While most detection algorithms rely on supervised learning and have achieved remarkable success with large-scale annotated datasets, the annotation process remains prohibitively expensive. As an efficient alternative, point annotations present significant advantages over bounding box and image-level annotations in terms of time efficiency. However, it remains an unresolved challenge to effectively utilise point annotations to enhance semi-supervised object detection. In this work, a Superior Point weakly semi-supervised DETR (SP-DETR) with teacher–student paradigm is presented for crop and weed detection. Specifically, a Point Amplification Module (PAM) is first proposed to connect point annotations to objects in many-to-one matching way. Next, dual parallel branches are equipped with point encoder to align the point annotation and input image semantically. Then, like-reference points and decoder queries are integrated into Denoised Decoder (DD) to establish stable Hungarian matching with fast convergence. Finally, Colour-guided Point Annotation (CPA) is employed to ensure accurate target identification against background interference. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of SP-DETR on BWD dataset when compared with other existing state-of-the-art approaches. In addition, ablation studies are carried out to verify the contribution of each proposed component. The source code is released to the public at https://github.com/731120464/SPDETR.

title: Pilot study on integrating multidisciplinary technologies to implement an autonomous and smart harvester for asparagus
abstract: Asparagus harvesting is physically demanding, often leading to back injuries caused by repetitive bending and tool uses. To address labor shortages, rising costs, and safety concerns, automated asparagus harvesters are becoming essential. This study developed an autonomous electric harvester incorporating multidisciplinary technologies to enhance efficiency and safety. The harvester utilizes rechargeable batteries to reduce reliance on diesel fuel, resulting in lowering carbon dioxide emissions. It also integrates mobility, image recognition, robotic arm, and clamping/cutting systems that employ mechanism designs, mechatronics, artificial intelligence (AI), and positioning control technologies. The mobile platform, powered by side-drive motors, autonomously navigates in asparagus fields. Two cameras equipping with AI-based image processing algorithm identifies asparagus spears ready for harvest. Experiments determined that a speed of 10 cm/sec was optimal for harvesting operation. This AI-enabled autonomous harvesting machine improves the efficiency of asparagus spears harvesting, reduces production costs, and advances asparagus farm management. It enhances competitiveness, secures labor availability, and maintains product quality in Taiwan’s asparagus sector, paving the way for large-scale cultivation.

title: Texture feature guided attention based fusion representations for crop leaf disease detection
abstract: The goal of automated crop leaf disease detection (CLDD) is to extract fine-grain visual features from images for classification. Vision transformers (ViTs) and attention-based models have improved classification accuracies by narrowing down the receptive fields of visual features, though often at the expense of computations and robustness. Generalizing visual features becomes difficult due to lacking diversification and overrepresentation of healthy leaves over diseased ones, causing overfitting and inherently limiting ViT’s capacity. Vision Transformers (ViTs) typically rely on single feature projection onto query, key, and value embeddings for self-attention calculations. In contrast, we introduce multi-feature projection. The texture representations extracted from RGB images are fed into key and value components, while the query takes RGB-coded features. Attention is the SoftMax-activated dot product computed on the three components. Simultaneously, a residual branch integrates RGB features with the attention vectors, producing moderately robust and interpretable compositions referred to as Texture Guided Visual Attention (TGVA) features. These TGVA features are integrated back into the backbone classifier network. Evaluating the Texture Guided Visual Attention neural network (TGVAnn) on the most challenging plant leaf datasets, sugarcane and maize, demonstrates its superior performance, achieving a 9% improvement in classification accuracy over traditional ViT models. Furthermore, TGVAnn shows a 20%–70% reduction in theoretical computational requirements (GFLOPs) relative to comparable baselines under a common reporting convention, supporting efficiency and scalability. This method outperforms similar approaches in both accuracy and robustness. In conclusion, the TGVA features derived from the multi-feature attention module effectively enhance the robustness of backbone image classifiers. This improvement is achieved with only a minimal increase in computational overhead of 13 M-parameters, making the approach both efficient and suitable for edge deployment scenarios.

title: Stages-based multimodal data fusion model(S-MDFM) for wheat yield prediction and screening of drought-resistant and high-yield varieties
abstract: Efficient and high-throughput prediction of crop yield and accurate assessment of varietal drought tolerance are essential for modern precision breeding and agricultural resource management and optimization. In this study, we propose a Stages-based Multimodal Data Fusion Model (S-MDFM) by integrating low-cost, high-throughput UAV-based multimodal imagery and multivariate data extracted from images. A staged error metrics (SEMs) propagation mechanism is constructed to capture the dynamic characteristics across growth stages and their dependencies with final yield, thereby improving the accuracy of cross-stage yield prediction (R2 = 0.8536, rRMSE = 16.12 %), validated prediction accuracy using data from the subsequent year in the same cropping area (R2 = 0.8370, rRMSE = 16.63 %). Based on wheat yield under varying water treatment gradients in drought stress experiments, the Drought Stress Tolerance Index (DSTI) and Drought Stress Susceptibility Index (DSSI) were employed to construct a Drought Resistance Index Differential (DRID) evaluation system. This dual-index approach enables multi-level screening of wheat varieties for drought resistance and quantitatively captures the synergistic relationship between yield performance and water adaptability and is capable of performing multi-level screening and quantifying the synergistic relationship between yield performance and water adaptability in wheat varieties, with an identification rate of drought-tolerant and high-yielding cultivars reaching 83.3 %. A multimodal fusion strategy based on discontinuous time-phase observations provides technical support for yield assessment and precise identification of drought-resistant and high-yielding varieties of wheat at different fertility stages, and the method provides a scalable multimodal data integration framework for varietal selection and breeding under drought-stressed field conditions, which is of great practical value for precision agriculture breeding applications.

title: A review of data-driven key technologies for intelligent citrus systems
abstract: In the era of the Internet of Everything, the construction of a digital citrus technology system that integrates digital, intelligent, and networked technologies is crucial for enabling efficient perception, cognition, and intelligent management of the complex systems encompassing citrus life, production, and ecology. Such an approach holds great significance for driving the intelligent transformation of the citrus industry. In view of this, this paper systematically discusses the concept and connotation of digital citrus, focusing on a comprehensive review of technologies such as environmental big data perception, omics big data integration, 3D modeling, intelligent breeding, and blockchain. It establishes a Citrus twin technology framework of “data perception − model construction − decision application.” From the perspective of industrial application, the paper summarizes the application effects of digital citrus technologies in tree shape optimization, growth monitoring, planting management, and brand building. Additionally, based on the technology framework, it elucidates the technical architecture of citrus big model. Lastly, it analyzes existing technological shortcomings and anticipates the development trends of key digital citrus technology systems in high-throughput and high-trust data closed loop, scalable AI-driven twin model, real-time decision synchronization, blockchain-based real-time traceability, aiming to promote the evolution of citrus production towards standardization, intelligentization, and sustainability.

title: Curvature sensing strategy for flexible gripper fingers during grasping deformation: enabling in-orchard online apple size grading
abstract: In-orchard apple size grading remains challenging under occlusions, variable illumination, and irregular fruit morphology. We present a contact–curvature strategy that integrates bending sensors into fin–ray flexible fingers to estimate fruit size during grasping, unifying grasp–and–grade operations. Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) reconstruction provides offline ground-truth curvature for calibration, yielding strong linear agreement between sensor readings and true curvature (R2=0.9852). Using temporal curvature features across approach, grasp, and steady phases, a gradient-boosting regression model predicts fruit diameter with R2=0.9577 and RMSE = 1.19 mm on the test set. In laboratory conditions, the system achieved an overall grading accuracy of 98.0 % for 200 apples classified into four grades, with a processing capacity of approximately 6 apples·min−1, meeting real-time requirements. In a small-scale orchard pilot study, the system maintainedR2=0.94 andRMSE=1.27 mm, achieving 96 % grading accuracy versus 77 % for a camera-only approach. Compared with vision-only sizing methods, contact-curvature sensing demonstrates inherent robustness to occlusion and illumination while better tolerating morphological irregularities. A methylene–blue protocol confirmed non–destructive operation. Contact–curvature sensing is robust to occlusions/illumination and can, in principle, extend to other near–spherical crops.

title: Integrating crop phenology and satellite data for improved nitrogen management in rice farming
abstract: Phenological heterogeneity is a key source of uncertainty in satellite-based nitrogen (N) management. Most existing N recommendation algorithms assume uniform crop development, which overlooks significant variation in crop phenology across regions and seasons, potentially affecting N application timing and efficiency. This study aims to develop a phenology-adjusted N recommendation framework for rice farming by integrating crop phenology monitoring with satellite-based vegetation indices using Sentinel-2 imagery. The shape model fitting based on separate stages (SMFs) method was employed to estimate the phenological progress and developmental stages of rice. Combining the sufficiency index algorithm (SIA), a phenology progress-adjusted SIA (SIPA) was constructed by aligning vegetation index reference curves with each field’s developmental stage to calculate the required N topdressing amount. Field experiments across Jiangsu Province, China, were conducted to validate the phenological detection and assess different N regulation strategies. Field-specific phenological progress maps for Xinghua City were generated, revealing substantial intra-regional variability in topdressing dates. The SMFs approach accurately predicted key phenological stages, with root mean square errors ranging from 2.35 to 6.85 days across diverse sites. SIPA reduced N recommendation errors by up to 70.2 kg · ha−1 compared to the conventional sufficiency index (SI). On-farm trials demonstrated that SIPA improved partial factor productivity of applied N (NPFP) by 10.39 % to 21.78 %, without compromising yield or net profit. SIPA also corrected misdiagnoses caused by phenological mismatches, especially in fields with early or late development. Integrating phenological progress into N management algorithms enhances agronomic precision and scalability. This phenology-informed approach advances sufficiency index methods and offers a scalable foundation for integrating crop developmental dynamics into variable-rate N management, with potential applicability across crops and regions pending further validation.

title: In-silico evidence for improving irrigated maize productivity in the Great Plains: A high-resolution spatial simulation approach
abstract: Food security and the depletion of water resources have become the two main concerns for the future of agricultural sustainability. Climate change, on the other hand, challenges global agricultural productivity, making target agricultural zones less productive. However, increasing yield potential through adaptation is crucial for improving global agricultural production. In this study, an approach for studying the impacts of future climate conditions and adaptation strategies on yield and water use dynamics of maize in the Eastern Kansas River Basin (EKSRB) of the US Great Plains, based on different future climate scenarios and deficit irrigation water management at a 4 km spatial resolution was presented. Using the spatially-adapted CERES-Maize model, the combination of impacts ofin silicogenotype-specific adaptations for selected genotype-specific parameters, treated as quantitative traits (improved canopy photosynthesis for radiation use efficiency [RUE], light extinction [KCAN], and heat tolerance [HEAT]), and agronomic management (shifting planting window [PD1 & PD2], and no nutrient limitation [NNL]) on yield and irrigation water use were explored. In addition, we assessed the integration of the individual genotype-specific and agronomic adaptation strategies to understand the co-benefits and trade-offs on yield improvement and water savings. Future climate scenarios for the region were created for two Representative Concentration Pathways (RCPs) (4.5 and 8.5) over three 25-year future periods (2025–2100) and compared to the historical climate (1991–2015). Results showed that future maize yield declined by approximately 34 % to 43 % (early and late century time periods, respectively) under RCP 4.5, and 33 % to 68 % (early and late century time periods, respectively) under RCP 8.5. Despite the yield declines, we found water use savings ranging from 9 % to 20 % (early and late century time periods, respectively) under RCP 4.5, and 13 % to 18 % (early and late century time periods, respectively) under RCP 8.5. We observed that integrated adaptation strategy linked to improved RUE, HEAT, KCAN, NNL, and PD2 (INT-NNL-PD2; Int 4), resulted in the early 21st century average yield gain of 0.6 to 3 % (RCPs 4.5 and 8.5, respectively), with water savings of 10 to 13 % (RCPs 4.5 and 8.5, respectively), relative to historical condition. However, going forward into the 21st century, we found marginal yield deviations (especially under RCP 4.5) with further increases in water savings, more than observed under the no-adaptation scenario. This suggests the need to re-examine and re-design these adaptation strategies for further yield improvement, while leveraging the benefits of water savings under future climate conditions. Our findings emphasize the transformative potential of all-inclusive integrated adaptation strategies in mitigating the impacts of future climate conditions on irrigated maize production in the Great Plains.

title: Emerging technologies for fast determination of nutritional quality and safety of insects for food and feed: A review
abstract: In recent years, insects have gained significant attention as a potential alternative nutritional source to address global food security and sustainability challenges. Commercial insect production is thus gaining traction and various insect species are being farmed for food and feed. Despite the increasing interest in commercial insect production and its promising future, there is still much room for improvement in terms of production efficiency. The profitability of insect production for food and feed relies on products' nutritional content, composition, and safety, which varies greatly according to insect species, diet, and development stage during harvest. Consequently, maintaining consistent nutritional composition of insect products require rapid and cost-effective methods for the determination of nutritional content and safety of insects. Additionally, a promising strategy for enhancing the nutritional quality of insect products may involve implementing selective breeding. This would necessitate employing nondestructive methods to measure the protein and fat content on all live selection candidates. This review paper presents a comprehensive study of the reference methods employed in determining the nutritional composition of edible insects. While highly accurate, the gold standard chemometric methods are widely considered to be costly, time-consuming, and destructive for determining the nutrition content. Our review paper therefore further extends to emerging technologies leveraging spectroscopy, computer vision, and spectral imaging tools 2 that promise fast and cost-effective prediction of the nutritional composition and safety of edible insects and insect products. The review paper also evaluates the suitability of these tools for predicting nutritional composition and safety of insect products providing examples of their applications in various contexts within the insect-based food and feed industry.

title: Two-stage contrast enhancement model based on HHO-CPM optimization and multi-objective evaluation for agricultural pests and diseases images
abstract: Agricultural pests and diseases image enhancement is critical for accurate identification and diagnosis. However, challenges such as uneven illumination and complex backgrounds degrade image quality, hindering automated systems. Traditional methods like histogram equalization lack adaptability to heterogeneous environments, while deep learning approaches face computational limitations in resource-constrained agricultural settings. To address these issues, this study proposes a two-stage image enhancement model integrating a customized Harris Hawk Optimization with Combined Perturbation Mechanism (HHO-CPM) and multi-objective evaluation, specifically tailored for agricultural pests and diseases analysis in smart agriculture. In the first stage, HHO-CPM was introduced to optimize the parameters in the image enhancement method and obtain elite candidate solutions. The HHO-CPM algorithm introduces improved exploration and exploitation position update formulas, attaining a relative equilibrium between global search and local search through a dynamic adaptive shift parameter. A combined perturbation mechanism helps the algorithm overcome local stagnation. In the second stage, a weighted evaluation function was designed to combine PSNR, FSIM, and MSE metrics, ensuring robust quality assessment. The effectiveness and superiority of the proposed model were evaluated through a series of experiments on real-world engineering problems and agricultural pests and diseases grayscale and color image enhancement problems. The findings demonstrate that HHO-CPM achieves highly promising results for both complex practical optimization problems and image enhancement problems compared to other optimization algorithms and image enhancement methods. The two-stage contrast enhancement model harmonizes numerical optimization with perceptual quality metrics, offering a pragmatic solution for pests and diseases diagnosis. This work advances adaptive image preprocessing techniques, bridging the gap between algorithmic optimization and practical agricultural applications.

title: EFNetPX: An improved panoptic perception network for inter-row navigation in orchard
abstract: Drivable area segmentation and obstacle detection are critical for inter-row navigation in orchards. However, existing methods typically address these tasks independently, leading to increased computational requirements. In this study, we proposed a novel panoptic perception network, EFNetPX, that integrates drivable area segmentation and obstacle detection tasks. First, we constructed an orchard dataset containing 1335 images featuring various fruit trees and obstacles. Additionally, based on YOLOPX, we enhanced the backbone with the improved EfficientFormerV2, introduced a BiFPN neck, and applied Powerful-IoU loss function. EFNetPX’s anchor-free design improves generalization across orchard scenes. Finally, the RANSAC algorithm was applied to extract the navigation line based on the semantic segmentation results, combined with the obstacle information to assess driving safety. EFNetPX improved CPU inference speed from 4.93 frames per second (FPS) to 8.03 FPS, while obtaining a mean average precision (mAP) of 93.92 % and a mean intersection over union (mIoU) of 97.21 %, with results comparable to the baseline model (93.37 % mAP, 97.26 % mIoU). Notably, introducing the trunk detection task improved the mIoU value by approximately 7 percentage points compared to pure semantic segmentation networks such as STDC. The attitude error and distance error of line extraction on 640 × 360 resolution images were within 1.19 degrees and 6.96 pixels, respectively—representing reductions of 41.82 % and 39.24 % compared to results based on trunk detection. This improvement significantly enhanced navigation robustness in complex environments. The proposed method could provide an effective environment-aware solution for agricultural robotics applications.

title: MPCD: A multimodal prior and conditional detection framework for High-Fidelity pest image generation
abstract: Automatic pest image segmentation is crucial for pest detection and recognition, but challenges persist because of irregular images and low contrast between pests and their surroundings. Pest identification is difficult because of the small size of pests and complex backgrounds, which can hinder accurate feature extraction. The key is to create a model that detects and transforms these regions for attention and discriminative learning. Therefore, a novel pest image synthesis framework called multimodal prior and conditional detection (MPCD) is proposed to overcome the difficulties of multimodal misalignment, fine-grained morphological ambiguity, and detail degradation. First, an object component prediction module that breaks down pest instances into relational graphs and part-level representations is used to extract structured visual priors. Second, under the direction of a gated hybrid mixing module, these priors are encoded and improved via a multimodal feature fusion process that combines semantic content with edge information. Finally, a sparse Transformer module is developed to capture long-range dependencies and highlight important structural cues during picture synthesis to improve spatial consistency and provide visually coherent outcomes. Experiments show that MPCD outperforms current methods, achieving a Fréchet inception distance (FID) of 20.11 and a contrastive language–image pretraining (CLIP) score of 0.3276. It has a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 26.26 dB and a structural similarity index measure of 82.65 % in detail enhancement tasks on the IP102 dataset. Meanwhile, MPCD obtains FID of 24.65 and a CLIP score of 0.3025 on the Agricultural Pest dataset. Ablation studies confirm the module’s individual and collaborative benefits. Qualitative visualizations show superior pest morphology generation across life stages and species ambiguities.

title: Estimating small-grain cereal plant density at early growth stages using leaf tip density dynamics derived from submillimeter-scale RGB imagery
abstract: Plant density is an important variable for management and phenotyping of small-grain cereal crops such as wheat and barley. While many image-based estimation methods exist to replace laborious manual counting, most of them rely on empirical relationships that may not generalize well to different sites, growth stages, species and varieties. In this study, we propose a novel small-grain cereal plant density estimation method that uses leaf tip density dynamics derived from submillimeter-scale images acquired at 45° view zenith angle. This method contained two steps. In the first step, a P2PNet deep learning detection model was trained to estimate leaf tip count in a surface of known area to get the leaf tip density. An occlusion correction method was then applied on this density, leading to an estimation error of about 20% at critical growth stages. In the second step, a wheat leaf dynamic model was used to simulate the evolution of leaf tip density over thermal time as functions of several variables, including mean time of plant emergence, phyllochron and plant density. This model was then inverted using a lookup table approach to estimate plant density from leaf tip density dynamics. The results obtained on three test datasets indicated that two observations performed before the appearance of the second and third leaves could be sufficient to attain a relative plant density estimation error of about 10%. We also discussed that this method should be able to work on other datasets without recalibration, and estimate other variables such as phyllochron at early growth stages. The code will be available at: https://github.com/wdwzytc/WheatPlantDensity.

title: UAV-assisted scan planning for improved forest inventory using a mobile backpack LiDAR system
abstract: Recent advancements in laser scanning technology have significantly improved data acquisition efficiency for obtaining forest biometrics. However, scan planning in forest environments remains largely dependent on in-field decisions by forest inventory personnels, often resulting in inefficient and less than ideal outcomes. To address this challenge, this study proposes an automated framework for determining optimal scan plans for mobile backpack Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) systems, leveraging a point cloud derived from an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) LiDAR system as prior knowledge. The proposed framework comprises three primary phases: (1) generation of scan-path candidates based on the navigable space; (2) optimization of scan coverage through 3D visibility simulation; and (3) path planning using a clustered traveling salesman problem (CTSP) optimization. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving a Lack of Completeness (LoC) of 1.4 % in plantation forests and 14.4 % in more complex natural forest environments. Additionally, the proposed method significantly reduces scan operation time compared to traditional manual approaches by inventory personnel while maintaining or substantially improving scan coverage quality. Future work will focus on integrating this framework with real-time navigation systems to further enhance operational efficiency and promote autonomous under-canopy forest inventory mapping.

title: Editorial Board
